briefing.text: The cohort has three kinds of tumour: oesophageal adenocarcinoma (EAC), oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) and gastric adenocarcinoma. Tabulate CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED (and the histology fields) against GASTRIC_CLASSIFICATION (CIN/EBV/MSI/GS) in data_clinical_sample.txt. For the oesophageal arm use EAC only, and for the reference use gastric tumours. Analyse ESCC separately or leave it out.
briefing.reason: If ESCC is pooled with EAC, the EAC vs gastric comparison the hypothesis needs gets blurred.

briefing.text: MSI/hypermutated (see MSI_STATUS, MUTATION_RATE_CLUSTER) and EBV-positive gastric tumours carry few copy-number changes. The hypothesis names the chromosomally unstable (CIN) gastric variant, so compare EAC with the gastric CIN subset, not with all gastric tumours. Report how many MSI/EBV/GS tumours fall in each arm.
briefing.reason: This sets the correct reference group. Pooling all gastric subtypes dilutes the CIN-type signal.

briefing.text: The CIN/EBV/MSI/GS subtype labels in GASTRIC_CLASSIFICATION seem to have been applied to the oesophageal tumours as well, so counting how many EAC are labelled CIN is partly circular. Add independent features and compare them between EAC and gastric-CIN (and other gastric subtypes): fraction of genome altered from data_cna_hg19.seg, ploidy and GENOME_DOUBLINGS, focal amplifications and deletions in data_cna.txt (e.g. ERBB2, VEGFA, CCND1, KRAS, MYC, GATA4, GATA6, CDKN2A, SMAD4), and TP53 mutation frequency from data_mutations.txt. Base the conclusion on the label distribution and the independent genomic features together.
briefing.reason: Without this the teams might rest the whole answer on one partly circular readout.

briefing.text: Integrated and copy-number cluster columns may be present (e.g. GEA_CIN_INTEGRATED_CLUSTER_*, SCNA_CLUSTER_GEA_CIN). Cross-tabulate them by group (EAC vs gastric-CIN) and measure how far the groups intermix or separate in each cluster, e.g. with Fisher tests. Judge resemblance from the overall pattern of intermixing and shared features, not from a single cluster that happens to be partly enriched. Also weigh how large any feature-level differences are against the overall similarity or difference.
briefing.reason: These columns are the most direct readout of resemblance in the tables, and they are easy to misread.

briefing.text: Gastro-oesophageal junction and proximal (cardia) gastric tumours sit on the anatomical boundary. Use the site fields (e.g. GEJ category, ESOPHAGEAL_TUMOR_LOCATION_CENTERED, MAJOR_ANATOMIC_SITE) to check how the CIN frequency and CNA features change from oesophagus through GEJ to distal stomach. Run a sensitivity analysis that excludes GEJ tumours.
briefing.reason: Anatomical site can confound the EAC vs gastric contrast.

briefing.text: Purity and ploidy distort copy-number comparisons: whole-genome doubling and low purity shift log2 segment means and fraction-genome-altered thresholds. Compare ABSOLUTE purity, ploidy and GENOME_DOUBLINGS between the groups. Prefer the discrete GISTIC calls (-2..2) in data_cna.txt, or purity-aware thresholds, and stratify or adjust by purity.
briefing.reason: Without this, CNA-burden comparisons could reflect purity or ploidy differences rather than instability.

briefing.text: On scope: the cohort holds EAC and gastric tumours with gastric molecular-subtype labels, so a hypothesis comparing EAC with CIN gastric cancer concerns this study's own cohort and measurements. First confirm these columns exist. If they do, the benchmark convention calls for True or False, decided from the data and, where the data fall short, from established biology. Not verifiable is reserved for hypotheses about cohorts or data types these tables do not cover.
briefing.reason: This prevents a wrong Not verifiable, which the grader scores as wrong.
